title: Inverse Square Law 3D Visualization
full_prompt:
Write a ManimGL script using the InteractiveScene class that visualizes the Inverse Square Law in 3D. 

1. Setup a 3D scene with a central light source represented by a GlowDot and a wireframe sphere of radius 2 using Sphere and SurfaceMesh.
2. Create an outward-emanating light radiation effect. This should be achieved by replicating a portion of the sphere, scaling it outwards, and animating its opacity using a custom beaming_effect helper and a ValueTracker.
3. Highlight a small parametric patch on the sphere's surface (e.g., u from 0 to 9 degrees, v from 90 to 99 degrees) and project a beam of light through it.
4. Rotate and reorient the camera dynamically to capture the 3D perspective.
5. Scale the sphere and the patch by a factor of 2 to demonstrate how the same light energy spreads over 4 times the area. Show grid divisions on the scaled-up patch using ParametricCurves to visually represent the 4x area increase.
6. Ensure proper 3D rendering depth sorting using always_sort_to_camera.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing always_sort_to_camera call causing 3D transparency rendering artifacts
common_failure_modes.note: Without proper sorting, overlapping transparent 3D surfaces will render out of order.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect camera reorientation parameters leading to sudden jumps or out-of-frame objects
common_failure_modes.note: The camera reorient method requires precise angles and target coordinates to keep the sphere centered.
